newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Russian news sinks De Beers shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian news sinks De Beers shares.

text.p: De Beers stocks plunged in early trade with big sellers baling out of the share following diamond giant's ultimatum that the Russians sign a new marketing deal by the end of the year, dealers said.
Shares fell to 121.75 rand from an opening price of 128 rand before recovering slightly to 123 rand by 0845 GMT. It was the third biggest loser on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"It is falling badly on the Russian news which is the biggest influence. The guys are all big sellers. Chartists are talking about it falling to 100 rand," a dealer said.

De Beers announced on Wednesday that it would cease to buy Russian stones under an old agreement from December 31. It said a memorandum of understanding for a new deal, which had been signed last February, had to be ratified by the end of the year. Failing that, no agreement would be in place.
Dealers said that 122 rand a share was the stock's first support level, which it briefly broke through.
They said 115 rand a share was the next support and if that went it could go all the way down to 100.
Volumes were fairly large for morning trade with 85,800 shares changing hands.

De Beers also announced dazzling 1996 diamond sales figures of $4.834 billion on Wednesday, but that that news was completely overshadowed by fears that De Beers could lose another chunk of its empire if Russia left for good.
